text:
**For a full recharge in one day, plan on roughly 270-340 W of panels (about 300 W). A 200 W panel will do it in about a day and a half.**

## The math
Panel watts ≈ battery Wh ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75). The 0.7-0.75 factor covers heat, panel angle, and charge-controller losses ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts for 1,000 Wh in one day |
|---|---|
| 3 (winter or cloudy) | ~450 W |
| 4 | ~340 W |
| 5 | ~270 W |
| 6 (summer, Southwest) | ~230 W |

Source: [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/). Another guide puts a 1,000 Wh refill at about 300 W in summer and 700 W or more in a northern winter ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

## If you'd rather use a smaller panel
- **100 W** gives about 315 Wh/day, so roughly 3 days.
- **200 W** gives about 630 Wh/day, so roughly 1.5 days. The rule of thumb is battery Wh ÷ 5 for a day and a half of decent sun ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/), [Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station)).
- **400 W** gives about 1,260 Wh/day, so under a day, if the station accepts it.

## Check before buying
- **Station solar input limit:** Panels above the limit add nothing. Many 1,000 Wh units cap at 200-800 W, so look up your model's spec.
- **Voltage:** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside the station's input range. Series wiring adds voltage and can damage the station. Parallel is the safer default.
- **Using power while charging:** Your load is subtracted from the solar input, so recharging takes longer.
- **Aiming the panel:** Tilting it toward the sun can add 20-30%.
